item.title: Why Are Pakistan’s Powerful Generals Panicking Over an Op-ed Article?
item.description: In a climate of economic and political uncertainty, even a single article in a newspaper with a modest circulation is now viewed as a potential spark for mass unrest.

item.title: An Alliance of Political Newcomers Seeks to End Old Parties’ Monopoly in Nepal
item.description: A popular mayor, a former TV star and an ex-chief of Nepal’s electricity board have joined hands to fight the old guard in the upcoming elections.

item.title: Why Strengthening RFA Is a Strategic Imperative for US Policy on North Korea
item.description: Expanding access to independent information is essential for U.S. security interests, human rights objectives, and long-term regional stability.

item.title: Why Beijing Won’t Be Emboldened by the ‘Venezuela Precedent’
item.description: China’s coercion threshold is set by its own internal logic – not by external “precedents.”

item.title: Kyrgyz Deputy Prime Minister Suggests a Review of Visa-Free Scheme for Americans
item.description: Following the imposition of visa bonds for Kyrgyz travelers to the United States, a Kyrgyz politician has suggested Bishkek reassess its visa-free program for Americans.

item.title: How Social Media Transparency Strengthens Geopolitical Stability in East Asia
item.description: The simple step of displaying geographic locators has pulled back the curtain on foreign disinformation operations in Japan and Taiwan.

item.title: Lee’s First Visit to Beijing: A Nuanced Restoration of China-South Korea Ties
item.description: Seoul and Beijing are back on track in reviving their bilateral ties, while conveying their own messages on the North Korea and Taiwan issues.

item.title: Is the US Air Force’s Quicksink Bomb the ‘Silver Bullet’ to Blunt a Taiwan Invasion?
item.description: The USAF’s B-2 or B-21 stealth bombers, armed with large numbers of cheap Quicksink bombs, could wreak havoc on a Chinese invasion fleet.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reimposes Gas Station Restrictions
item.description: For the second time in a month, Uzbek authorities have restricted hours at methane filling stations due to a drop in gas pipeline pressure.

item.title: Umar Khalid and the Erosion of Indian Justice
item.description: Khalid’s case is a stark example of how the Modi government weaponizes anti-terror laws to indefinitely silence Muslim voices and crush dissent.
